title: Car Fleet
hints: a car's fleet membership only depends on cars starting ahead of it, not behind - so what order should you process cars in, and what single number captures whether a car merges into the fleet ahead of it?
compute, for every car, the time it would take to reach target on its own: (target - position) / speed

sort cars by starting position in descending order (closest to target first), and think of the answer as a stack of 'fleet arrival times', where the top of the stack is the most recently formed fleet's arrival time

process cars from closest to target to farthest: if the current car's own arrival time is greater than the time on top of the stack, it can never catch up, so it forms a new fleet - push its time. otherwise it merges into the fleet ahead (its own time is discarded, since it arrives no later than that fleet)
commonMistakes: sorting by speed instead of by starting position, which breaks the 'closest to target first' processing order the algorithm relies on
comparing a car's arrival time to the immediately previous car's time instead of to the most recent surviving fleet's time (which may belong to a car further away after merges)
using <= instead of < (or vice versa) when deciding whether a car merges, which can misclassify cars that arrive at exactly the same time as a genuinely separate fleet

content.problemStatement:
A number of cars are driving toward the same destination, `target`, along a single-lane road, so cars can never pass one another. Each car has a starting position (all strictly less than `target`) and a constant speed.

**If a faster car catches up to a slower car ahead of it before reaching `target`, they merge and travel together as one fleet, from then on moving at the slower car's speed. Return the number of distinct fleets that will eventually arrive at `target`.**
constraints: all values in position are distinct
notes: a single car (always exactly one fleet)
every car moves at exactly the speed needed to merge with the one ahead
cars that never catch up to anything, each arriving as its own fleet
